title: Watch the Copy Constructor Fire
prompt_md:
## Goal
Define a class whose copy constructor announces itself, so you can see exactly when a copy happens when an object is passed by value.

## The feature (lesson 14.14)
Write a copy constructor for `Message`. The copy constructor takes a `const Message&` source, copies its `m_id`, and prints a line each time it runs so copies become observable. Passing a `Message` by value to `deliver` is what triggers it.

## Input
- Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10)
- Next `N` lines: one integer id per line

## Output
For each id, in order: first the line printed by your copy constructor when the object is copied into `deliver`, then the line `deliver` prints. The copy-constructor line must be exactly `copy <id>` and `deliver`'s line is `deliver <id>`.

test_cases.label: Hidden: four messages
test_cases.expected_stdout:
copy 7
deliver 7
copy 0
deliver 0
copy 13
deliver 13
copy 100
deliver 100

title: By Value vs By Reference
prompt_md:
## Goal
Use a self-announcing copy constructor to prove that passing by value copies an object while passing by `const` reference does not.

## The feature (lesson 14.14)
Write the copy constructor for `Widget`. It copies `m_id` from its `const Widget&` source and prints a line so each copy is visible. The provided `byValue` function takes its parameter by value (a copy happens); `byRef` takes a `const Widget&` (no copy happens).

## Input
- Line 1: integer `N` (1 ≤ N ≤ 10)
- Next `N` lines: one integer id per line

## Output
For each id, in order: `byRef` runs first and prints `byRef <id>` with no copy. Then `byValue` is called: your copy constructor prints `copied <id>`, after which `byValue` prints `byValue <id>`.

test_cases.label: Sample: two widgets
test_cases.expected_stdout:
byRef 7
copied 7
byValue 7
byRef 3
copied 3
byValue 3

test_cases.label: Hidden: three widgets
test_cases.expected_stdout:
byRef 50
copied 50
byValue 50
byRef 0
copied 0
byValue 0
byRef 99
copied 99
byValue 99
